title: Whole cell protein extraction and Western blotting
author: Isabel Lam

steps_raw.instruction: Whole-cell protein extraction and Western blotting Author: Alain Ndayisaba Khurana Lab, Brigham and Women’s Hospital 1. Purpose This protocol describes cell lysis for whole-cell protein extraction followed by western blotting using LI-COR Odyssey quantitative western blot. Frozen cell pellets described here are typically iPSC-derived cortical neurons, seeded into a 24 well plate format at 1x10^6 cells per well, and collected for downstream processing at DIV25. 2. Materials iBlot 2 Gel Transfer Device (Thermo Fisher) Odyssey CLx Infrared Imager (LI-COR) 3. Reagents NuPage™ LDS sample buffer (Life Technologies, Cat. # NP0007) cOmplete™ EDTA-free Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (Sigma Aldrich, Cat. # 11873580001) PhosSTOP phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Sigma Aldrich, Cat. # 4906845001) Pierce™ BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher, Cat. # 23227) NuPAGE 4-12% Bis-Tris protein gels (Life Technologies, Cat. # NP0322BOX) NuPAGE MES SDS Running Buffer (Life Technologies, Cat. # NP000202) 4% Paraformaldehyde (Thermo Scientific, Cat. # 28906) LI-COR Odyssey blocking buPer (PBS) (Fisher Scientiﬁc, Cat. # NC9877369) Tween-20 (Fisher Scientiﬁc, Cat. # 50213612) Primary antibody IRDye secondary antibody (Li-COR): e.g., IRDye® 800CW (LI-COR Biosciences, Cat. # 925-32214), IRDye ® 680RD (LI-COR Biosciences, Cat. # 925-68074) 4. Procedure 1. For cell lysis, thaw frozen cell pellets on wet ice 2. Resuspend cell pellets in 100 µL of 1X NuPage™ LDS sample buPer (diluted using dH2O) containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors. 3. Sonicate samples twice for 15 sec with a tip-sonicator at 40% power, keeping sample on ice. 4. Centrifuge samples at maximal speed for 10 min. 5. Transfer the supernatant to a new Eppendorf tube. Discard the cell pellet. 6. To quantify protein concentration, 5 µL of each sample was used in Pierce™ BCA Protein Assay Kit according to manufacturer’s guidelines.

a. Note: Add 5 µL of 1X LDS sample buPer containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors to bovine albumin serum (BSA) protein standards to account for LDS dye in absorbance measurement. 7. For western blots, set aside 30 µg of protein per sample for SDS-PAGE using NuPAGE 4-12% Bis-Tris protein gels in NuPAGE MES SDS Running BuPer. 8. Conduct electrophoresis at 150 V for 55 min or until the protein ladder and the loading dye indicate a suPicient electrophoretic separation. 9. Conduct dry transfer from polyacrylamide gel to nitrocellulose membrane with the iBlot 2 Gel Transfer Device using preset P0 program (20V 1 min; 23V 4 min; 25V 2 min). 10. If detecting alpha-synuclein, ﬁx membrane in 4% paraformaldehyde in dH2O for 30 min at room temperature with orbital shaking. Membrane ﬁxation improves alpha-synuclein detection (Lee et al. 2011 PLoS ONE). 11. Wash membrane three times for 5 min with PBS. 12. Block membranes in Li-COR Odyssey blocking buPer (PBS) for 1 h with orbital shaking. 13. Incubate membrane overnight in primary antibody solution, i.e. Odyssey blocking buPer (in PBS), 0.1% Tween-20 and the respective primary antibodies at the desired dilution, at 4°C with orbital shaking. 14. Wash membranes four times for 5 min in 0.05% Tween-20/PBS. 15. Incubate membranes with the secondary antibody solution, i.e. Odyssey blocking buPer (TBS), 0.1% Tween-20 and secondary antibody at 1:10,000 dilution, at room temperature with orbital shaking and protected from light. 16. Wash membranes four times for 5 min in 0.05% Tween-20/PBS. 17. Scan the blot using the Odyssey CLx Infrared Imager. 18. Use ImageStudio software for quantiﬁcation of bands. 5. References Lee, B.R., and Kamitani, T. (2011). Improved Immunodetection of Endogenous α-Synuclein. PLoS ONE 6, e23939. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0023939.
